Radiate

RAY-dee-ayt -- from Latin radius, 'ray': a feeling comes off you like rays from a source. · verb

Hear It

What It Means

To radiate to give off a feeling or quality you genuinely have, so clearly that no one can miss it.

The grandmother seemed to radiate warmth the moment she stepped into a room full of strangers.

Worked Example

A candidate walks onstage in front of a hostile crowd, and without raising his voice or hurrying a single word, he leaves the whole hall convinced he is not the least bit worried.

Giving off a feeling so plainly that everyone in the room picks it up -- here, calm -- is exactly what it means to radiate something. Unlike 'announce,' which needs words, radiating happens through presence alone.

How Radiate Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

show

show: to let something be seen

exude

exude: to give off a quality steadily and unmistakably

project

project: to send an impression outward to others

Antonyms

conceal

conceal: to keep something from being seen

suppress

suppress: to hold a feeling down and keep it in

How Strong Is It? — show → radiate → exude

show vs. radiate

show vs. radiate: Show is the plain, everyday version of radiate -- you can show annoyance with one frown, while to radiate a feeling is to give it off so steadily that everyone nearby senses it.

exude vs. radiate

exude vs. radiate: Exude is even more insistent than radiate: to radiate confidence is to give it off clearly, while to exude confidence suggests it seeps out of a person constantly, whether they mean it to or not.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — radi-

root — radi-: ray, beam, spoke of a wheel (Latin (radius))

suffix — -ate

suffix — -ate: verb-forming ending: to do or make (Latin (-atus))

Put it together

Put it together: Latin radiare meant 'to shine out in rays,' from radius, the spoke of a wheel or a beam of light -- when someone radiates confidence, the feeling spreads outward from them like spokes from a hub, the same root behind radius and radio.

Word Choice

Radiate has a literal sense (heat and light radiate from a fire), but on the ISEE it usually appears in its figurative sense: a person radiates joy, calm, menace, or confidence. This unit teaches only that figurative sense.
